publication_surface.identifier: Official Journal references of harmonised standards supporting Regulation (EU) 2016/426
publication_surface.authenticity_basis: Regulation (EU) 2016/426 Article 13 makes publication of a harmonised-standard reference in the Official Journal the condition for presumption of conformity with covered essential requirements.

dependencies.condition_statement: Presumption of conformity under Regulation (EU) 2016/426 Article 13 depends on conformity with harmonised standards or parts whose references have been published in the Official Journal.

scope.statement: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1750 formally decides not to publish the reference of EN 497:2022 in the Official Journal. EN 497:2022 therefore does not acquire Article 13 presumption-of-conformity status through OJ citation.

source_refs.locator: Article 1 — decision not to publish the reference to EN 497:2022
Article 2 — entry into force on the third day following OJ publication on 21 July 2026

forbidden_inferences: Publication or adoption of EN 497:2022 by a standards organisation by itself gives presumption of conformity under Regulation (EU) 2016/426.
A standard that is not cited in the Official Journal is legally equivalent to a cited harmonised standard under Article 13.
Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1750 is a textual mutation of Regulation (EU) 2016/426 Article 13.
Lack of Article 13 presumption of conformity means the standard is forbidden or that no alternative conformity route exists.
The formal non-publication decision may be collapsed into generic non-legal metadata.
notes: Third orthogonal Authoritative Dynamic Set regression for Candidate B. It tests formal prevention/non-publication of an OJ harmonised-standard reference rather than restriction of an already cited reference or addition to an agency list.
